title: Week 5 Mastery Quiz

questions.question: Which definition best matches “income tax”?
options: Credit that can be borrowed, repaid, and borrowed again up to a limit.
Interest calculated only on principal.
A tax based on taxable income under applicable law.
Property pledged to secure a loan.
questions.explanation: Income tax means a tax based on taxable income under applicable law.
choices: Credit that can be borrowed, repaid, and borrowed again up to a limit.
Interest calculated only on principal.
A tax based on taxable income under applicable law.
Property pledged to secure a loan.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “payroll tax”?
options: A transaction account designed for payments, withdrawals, and deposits.
A debt instrument promising specified payments subject to issuer risk.
A tax on wages used for programs such as Social Security and Medicare.
Property value minus debt secured by the property.
questions.explanation: Payroll tax means a tax on wages used for programs such as Social Security and Medicare.
choices: A transaction account designed for payments, withdrawals, and deposits.
A debt instrument promising specified payments subject to issuer risk.
A tax on wages used for programs such as Social Security and Medicare.
Property value minus debt secured by the property.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “sales tax”?
options: A contract granting temporary use of property under stated terms.
Preference for information that supports an existing belief.
A tax imposed on specified purchases.
The price paid for using borrowed money.
questions.explanation: Sales tax means a tax imposed on specified purchases.
choices: A contract granting temporary use of property under stated terms.
Preference for information that supports an existing belief.
A tax imposed on specified purchases.
The price paid for using borrowed money.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “property tax”?
options: A tax based on assessed property value, commonly supporting local services.
An interest-bearing deposit account intended primarily for saving.
A legally enforceable agreement requiring offer, acceptance, consideration, and other legal elements.
A credit check associated with an application that may affect scoring.
questions.explanation: Property tax means a tax based on assessed property value, commonly supporting local services.
choices: A tax based on assessed property value, commonly supporting local services.
An interest-bearing deposit account intended primarily for saving.
A legally enforceable agreement requiring offer, acceptance, consideration, and other legal elements.
A credit check associated with an application that may affect scoring.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “tax deduction”?
options: Interest calculated on principal plus previously credited interest.
Assets minus liabilities at a point in time.
An amount that reduces taxable income when allowed.
Failure to meet contractual repayment terms, often after specified delinquency.
questions.explanation: Tax deduction means an amount that reduces taxable income when allowed.
choices: Interest calculated on principal plus previously credited interest.
Assets minus liabilities at a point in time.
An amount that reduces taxable income when allowed.
Failure to meet contractual repayment terms, often after specified delinquency.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “tax credit”?
options: The amount a current sum is expected to grow to under stated assumptions.
Credit that can be borrowed, repaid, and borrowed again up to a limit.
An amount that directly reduces tax liability when allowed.
Return measured before adjusting for inflation.
questions.explanation: Tax credit means an amount that directly reduces tax liability when allowed.
choices: The amount a current sum is expected to grow to under stated assumptions.
Credit that can be borrowed, repaid, and borrowed again up to a limit.
An amount that directly reduces tax liability when allowed.
Return measured before adjusting for inflation.

The opposite conclusion is always true in every circumstance.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates mastery of the Week 5 inquiry?
options: A student selects an answer only because it sounds confident, even when the record is incomplete or contradictory.
A student accepts the first available claim or offer without checking the source, terms, evidence, or consequences.
A student applies each tax bracket only to income within that bracket and distinguishes withholding, liability, and refund.
A student relies on political identity, advertising, or personal preference as a substitute for documented analysis.
questions.explanation: A student applies each tax bracket only to income within that bracket and distinguishes withholding, liability, and refund.

shortResponse: What makes a tax system fair: ability to pay, benefits received, equal rates, equal sacrifice, or another principle?
rubric: 5 points: clear claim, accurate disciplinary reasoning, two specific pieces of evidence, meaningful qualification or counterargument, and complete explanation.
